STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 24 cm across the side. Treat it as a ~24 cm square, area ≈ 576 cm² (the plate is wide, so I use the full square area as the vessel; food covers only part of it).

STEP 3 - Items: (a) fresh spinach leaves, (b) shredded raw carrot. No dressing or oil is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Spinach covers about 30% of the plate (several large leaves spread over the right and centre). Carrot shreds cover about 2% (scattered strands plus a small heap under the leaves). Total food coverage ≈ 32%, consistent with the scattered look.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Spinach: 30% × 576 = 173 cm² × ~2.5 cm pile height (leaves piled and layered) ≈ 432 ml.
- Carrot: 2% × 576 = 12 cm² × ~1 cm ≈ 12 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Spinach: 432 ml × 0.15 g/ml ≈ 65 g.
- Carrot: 12 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 7 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Spinach: 65 g × 23 kcal/100 g ≈ 15 kcal.
- Carrot: 7 g × 41 kcal/100 g ≈ 3 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest plate of raw spinach with a few carrot shreds, about 70 g and roughly 18 kcal, is plausible for what is visible. Leafy greens are very low in energy, so the total stays small. Estimate is uncertain, mainly due to the leaf pile height.

Total: about 72 g, about 18 kcal.
